stem: Cell A2 contains "GLOBEX-2031-EUR". Which formula returns the issuer ticker "GLOBEX" and would still work for codes whose ticker has a different length?
explanation: FIND locates the first dash at position 7, so LEFT takes 7 − 1 = 6 characters. Because the length comes from FIND, the formula adapts to tickers of any length.

rationale.A: Correct. LEFT with a length based on the dash position returns the ticker for any length of code.
rationale.B: Incorrect. It works for GLOBEX but breaks for any ticker that is not exactly 6 characters long.
rationale.C: Incorrect. MID starting at the dash position returns text beginning with the dash, "-2031-".
rationale.D: Incorrect. RIGHT takes characters from the end of the string, returning "31-EUR".

explanation: EOMONTH moves one month forward from January to February and returns the last day of that month. 2024 is a leap year, so February ends on the 29th.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 15 Feb 2024 is what EDATE(DATE(2024,1,15),1) returns; EOMONTH returns a month-end.
rationale.B: Correct. The last day of February 2024, a leap year, is the 29th.
rationale.C: Incorrect. February has 28 days only in non-leap years; 2024 is divisible by 4 and is a leap year.
rationale.D: Incorrect. 31 Jan 2024 is EOMONTH with a months argument of 0.

stem: A1 contains the date 15 March 2025 and B1 contains 31 December 2025. What does =B1-A1 return when the result cell is formatted as General?
explanation: Dates are serial numbers: 31-Dec-2025 is 46022 and 15-Mar-2025 is 45731, so the difference is 291 days (16 left in March plus 30+31+30+31+31+30+31+30+31 = 275 for April to December).

rationale.A: Incorrect. 290 undercounts by one, as if the remaining days in March were 15 rather than 16.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 292 counts both the start and end days; simple subtraction excludes the start day.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 286 treats every month after March as 30 days (16 + 9 × 30) instead of using actual month lengths.

stem: D1 holds the date 30 June 2025, displayed as 30-Jun-2025. The title cell contains ="Report as of "&D1 but shows "Report as of 45838". Which formula fixes the title?
explanation: Joining a date to text uses its stored serial number and drops the cell's display format. TEXT converts the date into a formatted string first, giving "Report as of 30-Jun-2025".

rationale.A: Incorrect. VALUE returns the same serial number, 45838, so the title is unchanged.
rationale.B: Incorrect. DATE needs year, month and day arguments; DATE(D1) is invalid.
rationale.C: Correct. TEXT applies a date format inside the formula, so the label reads 30-Jun-2025.
rationale.D: Incorrect. CONCAT joins the same way as the ampersand and still shows 45838.
